results.title: On the trajectory of discrimination: A meta-analysis and ...
results.content: # On the trajectory of discrimination: A meta-analysis and forecasting survey capturing 44 years of field experiments on gender and hiring decisions. Discrimination against men for female-typed jobs remained stable across time. Forecasters failed to anticipate the stability of discrimination against men. A preregistered meta-analysis, including 244 effect sizes from 85 field audits and 361,645 individual job applications, tested for gender bias in hiring practices in female-stereotypical and gender-balanced as well as male-stereotypical jobs from 1976 to 2020. Forecasters correctly anticipated reductions in discrimination against female candidates over time. Instead, selection bias in favor of male over female candidates was eliminated and, if anything, slightly reversed in sign starting in 2009 for mixed-gender and male-stereotypical jobs in our sample. Forecasters further failed to anticipate that discrimination against male candidates for stereotypically female jobs would remain stable across the decades. ## Data availability. Preregistrations, data, syntax, and materials for Study 1 () and Study 2 () are available on the Open Science Framework.
